comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from VU Amsterdam's current official sources for 2026-2027: the Medische Natuurwetenschappen programme content page, the general programme page, and the programme's 2026-2027 Onderwijs- en Examenregeling (OER), Deel B2, Article 10.2 (afstudeerrichtingen: expressly 'n.v.t.', i.e. the programme has no formal specialisations), Article 11 (opbouw van het curriculum) and Article 11.3's complete year-by-year programme overview table with unit codes and EC weights for years 1-3, together with Articles 12.1-12.2 (vrije keuzeruimte and the approved minor list) and Article 9.1 (the bachelor-project admission requirement). Year 1 (60 EC) is common to every student: Inleiding MNW en mentoraat (3 EC, embeds a 0-EC diagnostic Dutch language test, VU_TAALTOETS, that is not itself a 180-EC component), Practicum Natuurkunde en Informatica 1 (6 EC, embeds a 0-EC lab-safety requirement, AB_LABSAFETY), Calculus (6 EC), Biochemie (6 EC), Medische (patho)fysiologie I (6 EC), Klinische en analytische chemie (3 EC), Mathematische methoden (6 EC), Organic Chemistry for MNW (3 EC), Fysica: Mechanica, Electriciteit en Magnetisme (6 EC), Natuurkunde en gezondheid (3 EC), Practicum bio-analytische chemie voor MNW (6 EC) and the capstone Project zenuw-werk (6 EC), which combines nervous-system lectures, brain dissection and programming. Year 2 (60 EC) is likewise common to every student: Moleculaire diagnostiek (6 EC), Basics of Bioinformatics and Systems Biology (6 EC), Thermodynamica (3 EC), Medische (patho)fysiologie II (6 EC), Differentiaalvergelijkingen (6 EC), Medische natuurwetenschappen en samenleving (3 EC), From Quantum to Molecule (6 EC), Optica en optisch waarnemen (6 EC), Statistiek voor MNW (6 EC), Practicum Natuurkunde en Informatica 2 (6 EC, embeds a 0-EC 'Studie en Loopbaan MNW' prerequisite, XB_000025) and the capstone Project kanker (6 EC). Article 10.2 explicitly records that the programme has no formal afstudeerrichtingen (specialisations/tracks): every student follows the identical major. Year 3 opens with a genuinely open vrije keuzeruimte of at least 30 EC (Article 12.1): a programmed minor (Article 12.2 names six approved options, including Minor Biomedische Beeldvorming and Minor Neurosciences), a free choice of units of education (at least 12 EC at level 300, at most 6 EC at level 100), study abroad on equivalent terms, or an internship; this space is preserved as open elective space rather than instantiated with invented content, consistent with its genuinely open, multi-option design. The remaining 30 EC of year 3 are fixed: Bachelorproject MNW (18 EC; Article 9.1 permits enrolment only once all year-1 and year-2 units are completed, with at most a 12-EC deficiency excluding practicals), Maatschappelijke en Historische Aspecten van de Natuurwetenschappen (6 EC), and one compulsory restricted choice of exactly one 6-EC unit from Machine Learning, Computational (Pharmaco)Chemistry, or Project systeemmodelleren voor MNW. This restricted choice is not a named formal route or specialisation (Article 10.2 confirms none exists); it is a single 6-EC curriculum unit that must be instantiated. Project systeemmodelleren voor MNW is selected because, unlike the other two options, it is a course-code specifically built for this programme ('voor MNW') that directly continues the programme's own year-2 systems-biology/systems-modelling thread (Basics of Bioinformatics and Systems Biology) rather than introducing a free-standing methodological or chemistry-specific skill; this selection was fixed before any UCR course was considered and does not depend on UCR fit. No OER article or further official source needed to be consulted beyond the programme content page and the OER itself: together they establish a complete, internally consistent 180-EC pathway with explicit EC weights and compulsory/restricted-choice status for every component.

alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to VU's Medische Natuurwetenschappen bachelor, which has no formal afstudeerrichtingen (OER Article 10.2) and instead integrates physics, chemistry, mathematics and computer science with human physiology and disease to prepare students for biomedical/medical-physics master's study. It combines UCR's full biomedical-science cluster (Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine; Human Physiology; Biochemistry; Molecular Cell Biology; Functional Anatomy; Mechanisms of Disease; Infection & Immunity; Pharmacology; Molecular Pathology & Genetics; Neurobiology; Life Science Laboratory; Epidemiology & Public Health) with UCR's full mathematical/computational cluster (Introduction to Programming; Mathematical Methods; Linear Algebra; Computational & Numerical Methods; Probability & Statistics; Introduction to Data Science; Machine Learning; Image Processing & Computer Vision; Neural Networks & Deep Learning; Database Management Systems) and Research Methods & Statistics. It reproduces VU's molecular and physiological disease core, its laboratory-research training and its research-methods/reporting sequence as far as UCR allows, and lets UCR's data-science and computer-vision courses stand in for VU's own imaging, bioinformatics and systems-biology content. It leaves VU's dedicated physics sequence (mechanics, electricity & magnetism, thermodynamics, optics, quantum-to-molecule physics) and its dedicated chemistry sequence (organic, clinical and analytical chemistry) as an honest gap: UCR offers no physics or chemistry course at all.

progressionAssessment.rationale: HCBGATE101 and DISGATE101 (both level-1 gateway courses with no prerequisite of their own) are scheduled in semester 1, and DISGATE102 (also a level-1 gateway course) is scheduled in semester 2, before any course that formally requires them: every HCBLIFE/HCBBIOM/HCBCOGN course that lists HCBGATE101 as a prerequisite is scheduled in semester 2 or later, and DISMATH211/DISMATH314/DISMATH213/DISDATA311, which formally require DISGATE102, are scheduled in semester 4 or 5, after DISGATE102 in semester 2. Level-1 courses are concentrated in semesters 1-2 (Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, Introduction to Programming, Introduction to Data Science, Mathematical Methods, Neurobiology, Research Methods & Statistics) and Epidemiology & Public Health in semester 5, so that foundational biomedical and quantitative training precedes advanced work. Level-3 courses are concentrated in semesters 3-6 (Pharmacology, Molecular Pathology & Genetics in semester 3; Mechanisms of Disease, Neural Networks & Deep Learning in semester 4; Probability & Statistics in semester 5; Infection & Immunity in semester 6), so that the disease-mechanism and advanced computational-methods work culminates after the physiological, biochemical and mathematical foundations are in place. Personal & Professional Development is scheduled in semester 1, within year 1. Every course is offered in its assigned semester under the fixed Fall 2026 cohort.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The closest match owns the seven generator-eligible rows that describe the programme's central, shared identity: developing technology for healthcare, combining physics, chemistry, mathematics and computing in medicine, understanding how disease works at molecular and physiological levels, medical diagnostics and imaging as a recurring application, translating fundamental science into clinical application, experimental laboratory research, and scientific research design and reporting. UCR implements this core through its full biomedical-science cluster and its full mathematical/computational cluster, standing in for VU's own integration of the exact sciences with medicine as far as UCR's actual offerings allow. The one remaining generator-eligible row, Biomedical Imaging (a stable study direction corresponding to VU's own Biomedische Beeldvorming minor), is assessed as its own candidate direction rather than folded into an omnibus bucket. However, VU's biomedical-imaging minor combines physics-based imaging instrumentation (optics, MRI/ultrasound physics) with image analysis, and UCR offers no physics or optics course at all: the only UCR courses that concretely address imaging or diagnostics content (Image Processing & Computer Vision, Neural Networks & Deep Learning, Functional Anatomy, Molecular Pathology & Genetics, Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine) are already the same courses the closest match uses to cover this evidence, because they are the only imaging/diagnostics-adjacent courses UCR's actual catalogue contains. Building a second 24-course programme around this candidate would therefore either reuse at least twenty of the closest match's own courses (far short of the required 30-EC/4-course floor) or substitute unrelated psychology/cognition or general-AI courses that are not evidenced by the biomedical-imaging interest row at all. Because the candidate's own evidence is already substantively covered by the closest match and no genuinely different 24-course curriculum follows from it given UCR's actual course offerings, it is rejected as not-substantively-distinct rather than manufactured through arbitrary course substitution, and production stops at one included alternative.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both are the introductory gateway unit that orients every incoming student to the field before any specialist course: Inleiding MNW en mentoraat introduces the programme and pairs students with a mentor; Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine is UCR's own entry point connecting cell function, health and biomedical science.

Practicum Natuurkunde en Informatica 1 is a joint physics-and-informatics laboratory practical. UCR offers no physics laboratory, but Introduction to Programming directly implements the practical's informatics/programming half (structured, object-oriented programming and computational problem solving); the physics-laboratory half is an honest gap.

Practicum Natuurkunde en Informatica 2 repeats the joint physics-and-informatics practical format in year 2. UCR's only programming course, Introduction to Programming, is already matched to the year-1 practical above and cannot be matched twice, so no further counterpart is claimed for this second, more advanced practical.

Both study the normal structure, function and energy handling of the human body. Medische (patho)fysiologie I is VU's first-year physiology course; Human Physiology is UCR's single physiology course and stands for VU's introductory physiology unit.
Both are the programme's dedicated biochemistry course, covering metabolic pathways, nucleic acids and biomolecules.

Both study how disease arises at the cellular and molecular level using concrete clinical cases. Project kanker is VU's year-2 capstone studying how cancer forms, is diagnosed and is treated; Mechanisms of Disease presents the cellular defects that trigger pathologies through clinical case studies, UCR's closest counterpart to a dedicated disease-mechanism capstone.

Both concern the structure and function of the nervous system. Project zenuw-werk combines nervous-system lectures, brain dissection and programming; Neurobiology covers nervous-system cell staining, microscopy and comparative anatomy, UCR's closest counterpart to a dedicated nervous-system course, though without VU's own programming component (matched separately to the physics-and-informatics practical).

Medische (patho)fysiologie II is VU's second, more advanced physiology course. UCR's single physiology course, Human Physiology, is already matched to the first-year unit above; UCR does not offer a second, more advanced physiology course, so no further counterpart is claimed.
Klinische en analytische chemie is a dedicated clinical/analytical chemistry course. UCR offers no chemistry course of any kind, so no counterpart is claimed.
Organic Chemistry for MNW is a dedicated organic-chemistry course. UCR offers no chemistry course of any kind, so no counterpart is claimed.

Both address the molecular and genetic basis of diagnosing disease. Moleculaire diagnostiek is VU's dedicated molecular-diagnostics course; Molecular Pathology & Genetics covers molecular pathology and human genetics, UCR's closest counterpart.

Both are hands-on wet-laboratory courses applying biochemical/biological laboratory technique to real material. Practicum bio-analytische chemie voor MNW is VU's bio-analytical-chemistry practical; Life Science Laboratory is UCR's laboratory-methods course, covering comparable data-mining and laboratory themes without the chemistry-specific instrumentation.

Both are the introductory mathematics course covering integration technique and equation-solving. Calculus is VU's first-year calculus course; Mathematical Methods covers the equivalent integration techniques, complex numbers and differential-equation solving at UCR.

Both are the programme's second, more advanced mathematics course. Mathematische methoden extends VU's quantitative training; Computational & Numerical Methods covers numerical methods, root-finding and the numerical solution of differential equations, UCR's closest counterpart.

Both are the programme's dedicated statistics course. Statistiek voor MNW is VU's statistics-for-medical-research course; Probability & Statistics covers probability theory, parameter estimation and statistical inference, UCR's closest counterpart.

Both concern the systematic computational analysis of large, heterogeneous datasets. Basics of Bioinformatics and Systems Biology introduces bioinformatics and systems-biology methods for analysing biological and medical information specifically; Introduction to Data Science teaches the equivalent general-purpose data-cleaning, visualisation and analysis skills that UCR offers in place of a dedicated bioinformatics course.

Both concern the capture and interpretation of visual/optical information. Optica en optisch waarnemen studies the physics of optical observation and measurement; Image Processing & Computer Vision studies the computational detection and interpretation of features in images, UCR's data-analysis counterpart to VU's physics-based optics course.

Differentiaalvergelijkingen is a dedicated differential-equations course. UCR's Computational & Numerical Methods, which covers the numerical solution of differential equations, is already matched to the more advanced Mathematische methoden component above and cannot be matched twice, so no further counterpart is claimed.
Thermodynamica is a dedicated physics course. UCR offers no physics course of any kind, so no counterpart is claimed.
From Quantum to Molecule is a dedicated physics course. UCR offers no physics course of any kind, so no counterpart is claimed.
Fysica: Mechanica, Electriciteit en Magnetisme is a dedicated physics course. UCR offers no physics course of any kind, so no counterpart is claimed.
Natuurkunde en gezondheid is a dedicated physics course applied to health. UCR offers no physics course of any kind, so no counterpart is claimed.

Both situate the natural sciences within a societal/health context. Medische natuurwetenschappen en samenleving addresses the societal, philosophical and ethical aspects of the natural sciences; Epidemiology & Public Health examines population health and public-health decision-making, a concrete societal application of medical science.

Maatschappelijke en Historische Aspecten van de Natuurwetenschappen is a dedicated history-and-philosophy-of-science course. UCR's only societal-context course, Epidemiology & Public Health, is already matched to the more directly comparable year-2 societal component above and cannot be matched twice, so no further counterpart is claimed.

The 30-EC year-3 vrije keuzeruimte (a programmed minor, an individual choice of units of education, study abroad, or an internship) is genuine open profiling space with no fixed content specified by VU. It is preserved as open space and not matched to any UCR course.

Bachelorproject MNW is the 18-EC independent bachelor research project. No scheduled UCR course is a thesis; UCR's standardised Optional independent research element is shown in this row instead, consistent with researchComponentId.

The restricted-choice unit is Project systeemmodelleren voor MNW, a computational systems-modelling project applied to a biomedical system. UCR's closest available quantitative/computational courses (Linear Algebra, Machine Learning, Neural Networks & Deep Learning) teach generic mathematical and machine-learning method rather than the specific applied biological-systems-modelling practice this unit requires, so no counterpart is claimed rather than treating a generic method course as a substitute.

comparator.text: Verplichte keuze: Project systeemmodelleren voor MNW
comparator.note: One compulsory restricted choice of exactly one 6-EC unit from Machine Learning, Computational (Pharmaco)Chemistry, or Project systeemmodelleren voor MNW. Project systeemmodelleren voor MNW is selected as the option most representative of the programme's own broad identity: it is the only one of the three built specifically for this programme and directly continues the year-2 systems-biology/systems-modelling thread, rather than introducing a free-standing methodological or chemistry-specific skill. This selection was fixed before any UCR course was considered.

notes.text: Both programmes include substantial study of human biology, disease mechanisms and mathematical/computational methods. The Medische Natuurwetenschappen bachelor additionally includes a full specialist sequence in physics (mechanics, electricity & magnetism, thermodynamics, optics, quantum-to-molecule physics) and chemistry (organic, clinical and analytical chemistry), taught through dedicated courses and laboratory practicals in every year. UCR students can instead combine UCR's biomedical-science and health-data-science courses, but UCR offers no physics or chemistry course at all, so those specialist components are not offered at UCR at any level of depth.
